answer: Use stake-backed delayed review: a new identity locks a deposit and is vetted by a randomly drawn panel of identities, whose votes appear only after the decision, so members cannot coordinate or be bought in advance. A panel approving a fake loses part of its deposit; a rejected applicant forfeits theirs. Trust widens like a spiral: a newcomer must first work in the meadow of participation, leaving an onyx record of votes and deposits that stays public. An attacker must fund a deposit and history for every fake, and corrupt several independent panels at once, so cost grows per added Sybil.
